messages:
sara: incident-bot flagged kvcache tier-3: sudden KV cache size explosion + continuous-batcher backlog. p99 tokens spiked, some in-flight requests 504-ing. noticing high mem pressure on inference-nodes-4..6. root cause TBD. paging eng-oncall.
incident-bot: ALERT: service=kvcache severity=high rule=cache-growth-bytes threshold=10gb window=5m host=inference-nodes-5
ops-bot: auto-scale attempted, added 2 nodes but they joined slow due to large cache sync.
tim: oncall here. saw the same. speculative-decode enabled at 02:10 for rollout on several models — wondering if draft/target sync is causing duplicate kv inserts?
maggie: quick customer-impact check: CS reports timeouts for three customers: Acme, NovaHealth, and FastShip (low-volume but high-QPS). No data exfiltration.
dustin: looks like continuous batching backlog amplified duplicate cache writes when speculative decoding retries created overlapping prefixes. We have a cache amplification pattern in logs: repeated upsert for same key range with different offsets.
leo: can we reduce batch window and disable speculative decoding on the serving tier while we triage? quick config change might mitigate.
sara: agreed. propose: 1) disable speculative decoding via feature flag on prod 2) set max_batch_tokens from 1024 -> 512 and reduce batching window from 25ms -> 5ms 3) clear small subset of hot shards to relieve mem pressure 4) keep autoscale but stop new joins from doing full cache sync (use warm-start).
tim: I'm going to flip speculative flag now on prod for all models configured with speculative. tagging @ops-bot for a config patch.
ops-bot: received. Applying patch: set service.speculative_decoding=false for cluster prod-kvcache. Rolling 3 control-plane workers.
(5m later)
ops-bot: patch applied to control-plane in 3/3. workers will pick up config gradually.
maggie: CS confirmed error rate dropped for FastShip to baseline, Acme and NovaHealth still seeing intermittent 504s — likely due to node OOM / GC thrash.
dustin: I'll start an emergency cache-evict on the two hottest shards instead of full clear. command: ```sh
# evict top keys with >100 write/sec
rdb-eject --shard inference-nodes-5 --criteria "writes>100" --dry-run
rdb-eject --shard inference-nodes-5 --criteria "writes>100"
```
leo: doing that now, starting with node-5. Also setting node join config to `cache_sync=warm` so new nodes won't trigger full replication.
sara: after evict we should also throttle continuous-batcher producers to avoid immediate re-populate. Put a short 200ms backoff on batch retries.
tim: applied batch config hotfix: `max_batch_tokens=512`, `batch_window_ms=5`, `retry_backoff_ms=200`. Rolling to 6/6 serving pods.
(3m later)
incident-bot: NOTE: p99 latency improved from 1.2s -> 320ms; error rate decreased 65%. Memory on node-5 dropping after evict.
maggie: CS says Acme still saw 1 outage window, but they received successful retries afterward. Put them on a follow-up incident response list for postmortem.
dustin: we're seeing residual KV divergence between draft and target caches — there are cases where speculative write ordering created keys pinned with draft tokens that weren't overwritten due to batch ordering differences. I'll capture diffs and export keysets.
leo: agree we need a deeper fix: either make speculative writes idempotent by including stable write seq or serialize speculative paths through the same KV write queue. Short-term mitigation: block speculative write path to cache (reads ok, writes to transient mem only).
sara: can ops make speculative writes read-only? i.e., write to ephemeral buffer not to persistent kvcache.
ops-bot: toggling speculative-write-mode=ephemeral on prod-kvcache.
(2m later)
ops-bot: speculative-write-mode is now ephemeral on 6/6 pods. Persistent kvcache writes from speculative decoder disabled.
incident-bot: p99 now 280ms; error rate further down 80% from peak. Autoscale stable.
maggie: Customer impact summary for pager: Acme had ~1.2k failed requests in 12m window, NovaHealth ~600, FastShip ~180. No PII leaked.
sara: immediate mitigation done. Actions: (A) full postmortem and RCA (owner: dustin) (B) follow-up hotfix to make speculative decoding idempotent and serialized (owner: leo) (C) add guard in kvcache to detect rapid upsert storms and reject on-policy (owner: tim) (D) add a canary test for speculative + batch interactions to CI (owner: eng-ml).
tim: creating infra task to add reject-on-storm policy and slow-path metrics.
dustin: exporting diffs and starting incident timeline. Will include logs: ```json
{ "event":"upsert_spike", "shard":"node-5", "peak_write_rate":1200 }
```
leo: rough timeline: 02:09 deploy enabled speculative decoding; 02:10 batch backlog formed -> duplicate writes; 02:15 alerts fired; 02:18 speculative toggled off; 02:22 hotfix batch config rolled; 02:26 shard evict started; 02:30 speculative writes made ephemeral; 02:36 p99 recovered.
maggie: I'll file CS follow-ups and draft a customer-facing incident notice.
sara: oncall handoff: tim hands to sara at 03:00 UTC for overnight monitoring. Please watch for regression if speculative re-enable is attempted.
tim: handing off. i've added runbook notes under /runbooks/kvcache-spec-decode/incident-1768504321.md and linked artifacts.
incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED (mitigated) at 1768504923. severity=high -> mitigated.
sara: thanks everyone. let's keep this thread for the postmortem comments and add logs + diffs when ready.
